risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: Difference GMM with internal lags is a standard but weak response to simultaneity (instruments unspecified, persistent series, Hansen p=0.097/0.110, AR1 p=0.056/0.146), so moderate is fair.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: Internet users and mobile subscriptions are standard proxies; the log descriptives (lnIU max 1.99, lnMS mean 6.90 in Table 2) are inconsistent with per-hundred units, so units are unclear but exposure is still captured.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: EU-27, 2002-2019 in 3-year averages; N=162 in Table 2 but 138 in Table 4 with no explanation, and Figure 1 lists the UK.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: Log GDP per capita is a level labelled 'economic growth'; price basis not stated.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: 18-21 instruments with no lag/collapse detail, no time effects, no robustness checks, large offsetting coefficients in interaction models (lnEI 3.83, lnIU -4.15), employment elasticity above 1.3.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: All four models are shown in full, but the conclusion emphasises positive ICT effects while ICT main terms are negative in Models 2 and 4; no robustness section.
risk_of_bias.why: Causal 'impact' language with a standard but loosely documented difference GMM, unclear variable units, an unexplained drop from 162 to 138 observations and no robustness checks; serious is defensible, moderate-to-serious borderline.

problems: No invented numbers found. Record matches the text on all coefficients, t-stats, diagnostics and instrument counts. Minor: the record says Table 2 lnIU/lnMS scales look inconsistent with per-hundred variables (true: lnIU max 1.99, lnMS mean 6.90). Text itself says GMM is 'Two-Step Difference GMM' (Table 4 note) while Sec. 3 cites Blundell-Bond; record follows Table 4. Authors' conclusion that ICT positively affects growth rests on Models 1 and 3 only; the Model 4 conditional mobile effect at mean trade is negative (derived).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: too_harsh: Baseline is country-FE with four controls and no year effects, but the authors discuss reverse causality and add a two-step system GMM with Hansen/AR(2) tests giving the same signs, which is a standard strategy (exogeneity not established), so moderate fits the guide.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: Mobile subscriptions per 100 and share of internet users are standard but not gender-specific.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: Unbalanced panel (638-862 obs); Appendix A countries are not classified by year and Appendix A omits labels that appear in Figures 2-5; 5%/95% trimming on the outcome.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: Male/female gross enrolment ratio, not net enrolment or completion; ratios below 1 mean girls ahead, so negative coefficients are not always 'less inequality'.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: No time effects, rounded coefficients (SE 0.000), turning points from rounded coefficients without tests.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: too_harsh: Non-significant results (internet-primary interaction, Q10 mobile-primary) are shown and variants are reported in full; the real issue is rounding and the text contradicting tables, which suggests low to moderate.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard FE panel with explicit causal framing, partly mitigated by a system GMM check and extensive robustness; per the guide this is moderate (exogeneity not established), not serious.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: System GMM with collapsed internal instruments, AR(2) and Hansen reported; instrument count and lags not given, the threshold variable is itself endogenous, and Hansen-style bootstrap search is combined with GMM without explanation.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: DIG mixes ICT with tertiary enrolment and schooling (overlapping the CAP control), and definitions conflict between Table 1/Sec. 3.2.2 (internet, mobile, payments, e-commerce readiness, WIPO) and Appendix B (six different indicators, no WIPO).
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 'Developing' list includes Chile, Uruguay, Romania, Bulgaria; a perfectly balanced annual 2000-2023 panel of survey-based Gini/Theil for 45 countries is hard to reconcile with data availability; 1,035 obs = 45 x 23 unexplained.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: Gini from WB PIP and Theil from 'ILO Labour Statistics; National Surveys' with no description of interpolation, harmonisation or income vs consumption basis; descriptive min/max values are unusually round (SUP 10.0/45.0, INF 30.0/80.0).
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: Single main specification, no time effects, no sensitivity to index weights or sample, bootstrap designed for static panels applied to a dynamic one.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: Table 7 (Theil) omits control coefficients and SEs; double threshold dismissed; no alternative exposure definitions.
risk_of_bias.why: Causal language ('exacerbates', 'mitigates') with a plausible system GMM, but the composite exposure overlaps with controls, definitions are inconsistent, and the balanced survey-based panel and round descriptives raise data-provenance concerns; serious fits, with a risk of critical if the data cannot be reproduced.

problems: Record error: it says China is absent from the sample, but China is listed in Appendix A (India is the one missing). Record phrase 'Mean years of schooling is 15+ in Table 1 and 25+ in Appendix B' refers to the population age group (aged 15+ vs aged 25+), not the schooling values; Table 4 gives CAP mean 7.82, max 13.00. The signs of Table 6 and 7 coefficients are lost in the converted text; record correctly flags that signs come from the prose. The record's claim that Schutz (1951) does not support the 'sensitive to middle/tails' statement cannot be verified from the paper text. Record locators for regime results cite p.60; Sec. 4.3.1 itself is on p.59. Otherwise numbers (Table 4 obs 1,035; Hansen 0.281/0.315, AR(2) 0.654/0.589; Theil Hansen 0.258 to 0.315) match.
